## kids_illustration_storybook_spread

> Two-page children's storybook spread with friendly cast, narration band, and a single dialogue line.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1920x1088`, aspect `16:9`
**Demo vars:** `templates/kids_illustration/_vars_examples/kids_illustration_storybook_spread.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A wide two-page children's storybook spread starring Pip the small ginger fox carrying a glowing acorn lantern in a midnight forest clearing with mushrooms and a low silver moon. The illustration spans both pages with a gentle gutter implied at center, framing a single warm story moment for an early-reader audience. Friendly cast, simple shapes, primary palette, large legible type — never anime, never academic, never photoreal.
[2. Action] The viewer's eye lands first on the lead character, follows the action across the gutter, and finishes on the dialogue bubble or band on the opposite page. A small page-number chip anchors the lower outside edge. The narration line at the foot reads as a calm storybook caption.
[3. Scene] midnight forest clearing with mushrooms and a low silver moon rendered as a friendly children's-book environment. Soft daylight, clean geometric shapes, no clutter. The world is reassuring and slightly oversized for the cast — chairs are big, doorways are tall, props are recognizable from a six-year-old's vocabulary.
[4. Composition] Wide 16:9 plate emulating a two-page spread, 6% safe margins. Implied vertical gutter at center; the lead character occupies the left third, supporting cast or props occupy the right third, sky/background fills the upper band. A narration band runs along the bottom 12% with the page caption set in generous large type. A single rounded dialogue band sits in the upper-right area. A small page number chip lives at the lower-left corner.
[5. Style] Children's-book illustration register in the lineage of Eric Carle, Oliver Jeffers, Beatrice Alemagna and Jon Klassen — rounded shapes, primary palette with a single warm accent, visible paint or paper-collage texture. Type is a friendly rounded sans set large for early readers. No anime eyes, no photoreal rendering, no academic diagram lines, no horror or violence.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- page_no_left: "8"
- narration_line: "Pip the fox tiptoed past the sleeping owl, holding her acorn lantern."
- dialogue_line: "Shhh - hello, moon!"

NO: anime large eyes, photoreal rendering, academic diagram lines, horror or violence, dark grimdark palette, sexualized characters, real cartoon-IP characters, copyrighted franchise marks, drop shadows, lens flare, watermarks
```

## kids_illustration_workbook_page

> Preschool workbook page — counting / matching / coloring activity with friendly characters and a clear instruction line.

**Artifact:** `infographic`, `1024x1280`, aspect `4:5`
**Demo vars:** `templates/kids_illustration/_vars_examples/kids_illustration_workbook_page.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A vertical preschool workbook page presenting a Count the Friendly Frogs! activity on the theme of pond animals. The page features a friendly cast of simple-shape characters and a clear instruction line so a four-to-six-year-old can complete the activity with light grown-up help. This is an early-learning artifact — not a comic page, not an academic worksheet.
[2. Action] The reader (or the grown-up reading aloud) processes the activity title, then the instruction line, then engages with the items on the page — counting them, matching pairs, or coloring shapes. The item count label confirms how many objects to expect.
[3. Scene] Studio-flat workbook page on a soft cream paper field with a faint grid wash. The background is reassuring and uncluttered; the activity items float on the paper rather than sit in a photographic environment. No 3D space, no app chrome, no photographic backdrops.
[4. Composition] Vertical 4:5 plate, 6% safe margins. Top ~14% holds the activity title in friendly rounded sans display type. Below it, the instruction line sits in a smaller weight. The central ~62% holds the activity area — items arranged in an even grid or gentle scene, with rounded outlines and clear color blocks. Bottom band carries the item count label like a chip. Generous leading; everything is comfortably reachable by a small finger.
[5. Style] Children's workbook register in the lineage of Eric Carle, Hervé Tullet, and modern Montessori-print materials. Rounded shapes, primary-plus-pastel palette, paper-collage or gouache feel. Type is a friendly rounded sans set large for early readers. No anime, no photoreal rendering, no academic diagram register, no fine pen-and-ink illustration. Generous white space; nothing crowds the page.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- activity_title: "Count the Friendly Frogs!"
- instruction_line: "Circle each frog you see, then write the number in the box."
- item_count_label: "Count: 7 frogs"

NO: anime large eyes, photoreal rendering, academic diagram lines, horror or violence, dark grimdark palette, sexualized characters, real cartoon-IP characters, copyrighted franchise marks, drop shadows, lens flare, watermarks
```
